a86.t:
The Bisley residents and ratepayers association in the Msunduzi Municipality in KwaZulu-Natal. From left, Njabulo Mnguni, Noluthando Mzobe (Chairperson), Hein van den Berg, Susan van den Berg, Ralph Raja (Deputy Chairperson), Ntsebo Mkhize (Secretary), and Nicholas Arokiam (Treasurer).
Image: Supplied
A woman has been elected to lead a revived ratepayer association in the Msunduzi Municipality, coincidentally during Women's Month.
Noluthando Mzobe was elected chairperson of the reconstituted Bisley residents and ratepayers association (RRA) on August 20.
This culminated after Bisley residents met in November 2024 to oppose the construction of a community hall, and it was decided to revive the Bisley RRA to engage the municipality on the proposed project, explained Anthony Waldhausen, the CEO of Msunduzi Association of Residents, Ratepayers and Civics (MARRC).
Waldhausen said several residents at the meeting volunteered to start the process to revive the RRA.
“The community came together in January this year to protest at the construction site and continued to picket at the site for over three months. It was found that the process for constructing the community hall was irregular and unlawful. It was through the residents’ protest that the project was halted and moved to the original site at Oribi Hall,” explained Waldhausen.
South Africa commemorates Women’s Month in August as a tribute to the women who marched to the Union Buildings on August 9, 1956, in protest against the extension of the Pass Laws to women.
Elevate Her.
Image: File
Mzobe said that she was honoured and humbled to have been elected as chairperson and that this is her opportunity to serve the community.
“I look forward to working in collaboration with the team and the community to address the needs of our neighbourhood. Together, I believe we can make meaningful progress and continue building a stronger and better Bisley for all of us,” she said.
Mzobe said her nomination came as a surprise because she joined the ratepayers association out of passion for keeping the Bisley neighbourhood safe and protecting it from bad developments.
“I did not realise my neighbours were watching and picking up some positive qualities in me. However, I am goal-driven; I like to see things through. Thus, I feel honoured to be elected as chairperson, and I wish to make the suburb of Bisley proud,” she said.
She was also proud of how women in leadership are growing and that she was now part of it.
“I am surrounded by a committee of very competent and accomplished men and women, and it’s truly exciting that the South African society is at a place where leaders are elected based on their skill and performance rather than gender preference,” she added.
Mzobe expressed her surprise at being nominated for chairperson by men.
“To see their confidence in me was also humbling. Also, such experienced men who are husbands and fathers saw a good leader in me due to my passion and organisational skills, and my being a woman was seen as a positive factor,” she said.
Mzobe was excited to start making a positive impact in the community.
Waldhausen said the MARRC will be available to provide ongoing support and training so that they are able to engage their ward councillor and address community issues with the broader community of Bisley.
“We are finding that residents are mobilising to get organised to address their issues and to hold the municipality accountable,” he said.
The committee also elected
• Deputy Chairperson: Ralph Raja
• Treasurer: Nicholas Arokiam
• Secretary: Ntsebo Mkhize
It also nominated Hein van den Berg and Susan van den Berg to represent the Bisley RRA on MARRC Exco as well.
The new committee will attend a workshop on the roles and responsibilities of office bearers to be facilitated by MARRC. Bisley RRA is the 13th civic association to join MARRC.

a130.t:
ZOMBA-(MaraviPost)-Minister of Youths and Sports, Uchizi Mkandawire on Thursday asked over 1000 Technical Entrepreneurial and Vocational Education (TEVETA) graduates from Mangochi and Zomba to embrace entrepreneurship in order to create employment for their fellow youths.
Presiding over the ceremony in Zomba, Mkandawire said the graduates can reduce unemployment level in the country especially if they start opening up their small scale businesses there by creating self-employment as well as employment for others.
Mkandawire said, “lt is President Dr Lazarus Chakwera’s version to see that many youths are equipped with technical skills and open up their businesses soon after graduation”.
To those without or with small business capital, Mkandawire said there is a room for them to obtain a loan from National Economic Empowerment Fund (NEEF) that President Chakwera initiated.
He then thanked the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) for its financial support of the whole initiative through Titukulane Project.
“As government, we want to thank USAID through its Titukulane Project for the initiative because it helped to equip the Youths with different technical skills. And to the graduates, please go and embrace entrepreneurship,” said Mkandawire.
In his remarks, TEVETA executive director, Elwin Sichiola while thanking USAID the country needs to have more programs like Titukulane Project.
Titukulane Project is aimed at providing technical skills to secure employment or start their own businesses in order to overcome poverty.

a281.t:
NAMIBIA SHINES AT CHINA EXPO
The minister used the opportunity to encourage exhibitors, highlighting the importance of quality, competitiveness and branding in succeeding on the global stage. Furthermore, she expressed Namibia’s readiness to attract foreign investment that can stimulate local industries and create sustainable economic growth.
The expo serves as a forum not only for showcasing Namibian products but also for networking and building partnerships with Chinese and other African business stakeholders.
Around 200 000 people visited the main exhibition hall.

a302.t:
Quelques mois après avoir quitté le pouvoir sans gloire, l’ancien président sénégalais Macky Sall revient en politique pour faire campagne à distance en vue des législatives de dimanche, au risque de l’incompréhension et du désaveu.
M. Sall, qui a quitté le Sénégal par la petite porte à destination du Maroc en avril, aussitôt après la passation avec son successeur Bassirou Diomaye Faye, a « accepté » de conduire son camp aux élections.
Depuis, la question de ses motivations est posée, comme celle des conséquences d’un éventuel retour au pays. Son ennemi juré, Ousmane Sonko, devenu Premier ministre, brandit à l’envi le spectre du procès pour juger les actes des anciens dirigeants.
M. Sall « a senti qu’il lui fallait une certaine prise sur le jeu politique pour protéger ses arrières » dans l’éventualité de « règlements de compte politiques », décrypte Maurice Soudieck Dione, professeur de science politique.
M. Dione envisage aussi une « dimension personnelle de non-satiété par rapport au pouvoir », en rappelant que M. Sall avait longtemps entretenu le flou sur sa candidature à un troisième mandat. Il avait renoncé et désigné son Premier ministre Amadou Ba pour défendre son héritage à la présidentielle de mars.
M. Sall a justifié sa décision dans une lettre de cinq pages par la nécessité de défendre les « acquis » de douze années de présidence et les « dangers » qu’encourraient l’économie et le démocratie au bout de moins de huit mois de gouvernance « calamiteuse ».
Le porte-parole de la présidence Ousseynou Ly a crié à « l’indécence » sur les réseaux sociaux, reprochant à l’ancien chef de l’Etat les morts de trois années de troubles, la dette et la corruption.
M. Sall, respecté sur la scène internationale, est parti réprouvé chez lui. Les dernières années de sa présidence ont été assombries par les retombées d’un interminable bras de fer avec M. Sonko. Des dizaines de personnes sont mortes, des centaines ont été arrêtées.
La soif de changement d’une population éprouvée par les crises nationale et internationales a fait triompher à la présidentielle le second de M. Sonko, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, sorti de prison en même temps que lui dix jours plus tôt.
En prenant aussi vite la tête de la coalition Takku Wallu Sénégal, M. Sall rompt avec la réserve traditionnellement observée, au moins provisoirement, par ses prédécesseurs.
Mais, tandis que M. Sonko écume le Sénégal en cortège et promet la transformation de leur région à des foules échauffées, M. Sall s’adresse via le haut-parleur d’un téléphone à des rassemblements moins tapageurs.
– Pardonner ou non –
Officiellement, M. Sall rentre quand il veut.
« S’il revenait au pays, nous assurerions sa sécurité parce qu’il est un citoyen et ancien président de la République », a assuré dans les médias Amadou Moustapha Ndieck Sarré, porte-parole du gouvernement. « Mais s’il revenait et que la justice décidait de son interpellation, ni le Premier ministre ni le chef de l’Etat n’y pourraient rien ».
S’il remettait les pieds au Sénégal, M. Sall ne serait pas sûr d’en repartir. Le Premier ministre Sonko revendique de bloquer la sortie d’anciens responsables.
M. Sonko a parlé récemment de « haute trahison » devant l’état dans lequel il dit avoir trouvé les comptes publics. La haute trahison est le seul cas où un président peut être mis en accusation.
« Foutaise », s’exclame dans le camp de M. Sall Abdou Mbow, l’un des vice-présidents de l’Assemblée sortante. M. Sonko « lui-même sait qu’il ne peut pas arrêter le président ».
El Hadji Mamadou Mbaye, enseignant chercheur à l’université de Saint-Louis (nord), doute que le nouveau régime aille jusqu’à faire juger M. Sall, parce qu' »au niveau légal ce sera très compliqué » et que M. Sall a « des flèches à son arc », qu’il pourrait diriger contre MM. Faye et Sonko.
M. Sall replonge en politique parce qu' »en réalité il n’a jamais voulu quitter le pouvoir », analyse M. Mbaye. « Il se sent indispensable ». Mais, ajoute M. Mbaye, il n’est pas « au centre du débat » et c’est son ancien dauphin présomptif et désormais concurrent Amadou Ba « qui s’est positionné comme chef de l’opposition ».
De là à pousser M. Sall à rentrer au pays… M. Sall a été pris à partie début octobre dans un avion Casablanca-Paris par une passagère sénégalaise qui lui a demandé en faisant référence à l’agitation des dernières années: « Pourquoi avez-vous tué nos enfants? », a rapporté la presse.
« Je ne pense pas que les Sénégalais soient (encore) prêts à pardonner », dit M. Mbaye.
« S’il était rentré, la campagne aurait été beaucoup plus mouvementée, à la limite violente. Il a eu à mener une répression très dure contre l’opposition. Les plaies ne sont pas cicatrisées », abonde M. Dione.
Avec AFP
a302.en:
A few months after leaving power without glory, former Senegalese president Macky Sall is returning to politics to campaign from a distance ahead of Sunday's legislative elections, at the risk of incomprehension and repudiation.

Mr Sall, who left Senegal by the back door for Morocco in April, immediately after the handover to his successor Bassirou Diomaye Faye, has "accepted" to lead his camp in the elections.

Since then, the question of his motives has been raised, as has that of the consequences of a possible return to the country. His sworn enemy, Ousmane Sonko, now Prime Minister, repeatedly brandishes the spectre of a trial to judge the acts of former leaders.

Mr Sall "felt he needed a certain hold on the political game to protect his rear" in the event of "political score-settling", explains Maurice Soudieck Dione, professor of political science.

Mr Dione also envisages a "personal dimension of non-satiety with regard to power", recalling that Mr Sall had long maintained ambiguity about his candidacy for a third term. He had given it up and designated his Prime Minister Amadou Ba to defend his legacy at the March presidential election.

Mr Sall justified his decision in a five-page letter by the need to defend the "gains" of twelve years of presidency and the "dangers" that the economy and democracy would face after less than eight months of "calamitous" governance.

The presidency's spokesman Ousseynou Ly denounced the "indecency" on social media, reproaching the former head of state for the deaths of three years of unrest, the debt and corruption.

Mr Sall, respected on the international stage, left disapproved of at home. The last years of his presidency were darkened by the fallout of an interminable standoff with Mr Sonko. Dozens of people died, hundreds were arrested.

The thirst for change of a population tested by national and international crises brought victory in the presidential election to Mr Sonko's number two, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, who had left prison at the same time as him ten days earlier.

By taking the head of the Takku Wallu Senegal coalition so quickly, Mr Sall breaks with the reserve traditionally observed, at least provisionally, by his predecessors.

But while Mr Sonko criss-crosses Senegal in convoy and promises the transformation of their region to excited crowds, Mr Sall addresses less boisterous gatherings via the loudspeaker of a telephone.

- To forgive or not -

Officially, Mr Sall may return whenever he wants.

"If he were to return to the country, we would guarantee his security because he is a citizen and a former president of the Republic," government spokesman Amadou Moustapha Ndieck Sarre assured in the media. "But if he came back and the justice system decided to arrest him, neither the Prime Minister nor the head of state could do anything about it."

If he set foot in Senegal again, Mr Sall would not be sure of leaving again. Prime Minister Sonko claims to be blocking the departure of former officials.

Mr Sonko recently spoke of "high treason" in view of the state in which he says he found the public accounts. High treason is the only case in which a president can be impeached.

"Rubbish," exclaims Abdou Mbow, one of the vice-presidents of the outgoing National Assembly, in Mr Sall's camp. Mr Sonko "himself knows that he cannot arrest the president."

El Hadji Mamadou Mbaye, teacher-researcher at the University of Saint-Louis (north), doubts that the new regime will go so far as to put Mr Sall on trial, because "at the legal level it will be very complicated" and because Mr Sall has "arrows in his quiver" that he could aim at Messrs Faye and Sonko.

Mr Sall is plunging back into politics because "in reality he never wanted to leave power," analyses Mr Mbaye. "He feels indispensable." But, Mr Mbaye adds, he is not "at the centre of the debate" and it is his former presumed heir and now competitor Amadou Ba "who has positioned himself as leader of the opposition."

As for pushing Mr Sall to return home... Mr Sall was taken to task in early October on a Casablanca-Paris flight by a Senegalese passenger who asked him, referring to the agitation of recent years: "Why did you kill our children?", the press reported.

"I do not think Senegalese are (yet) ready to forgive," says Mr Mbaye.

"If he had returned, the campaign would have been much more turbulent, bordering on violent. He waged very harsh repression against the opposition. The wounds have not healed," adds Mr Dione.

With AFP

a344.t:
A national initiative for the installation of billboards extolling biodiversity conservation and fostering nature-based tourism was launched in Maputo province on Monday, hosted by Ressano Garcia administrative post.
Seventy double-sided panels will be erected countrywide over the current five-year plan period, each costing 500,000 meticais, in an operation amounting to a total figure of 37.5 million meticais.
Minister of Land and Environment Ivete Maimbasse said at the event in Moamba that, in addition to spreading a message of environmental education and combating poaching and trafficking in wildlife products, the panels would promote wildlife and natural landscapes.
Also read: Mozambique: Campaign against poaching launched
“Today, we had the opportunity to witness the unveiling of the double-sided billboard, marking the start of the national initiative promoting biodiversity conservation and nature-based tourism,” the minister explained.
“These panels are vehicles of communication and mechanisms of social mobilization towards a greater individual and collective environmental awareness and for the massification of knowledge about the importance of changing behaviours in relation to the way we look at the biological resources that the country has,” Maimbasse said.
The billboards are also to be erected in the KaTembe municipal district, and in some parts of Maputo, such as the ATCM track.
A communication strategy for the conservation of biodiversity was also launched at the Ressano Garcia event, as an instrument for the sustainability of the country’s wildlife and forest resources.
Mateus Mutemba, director-general of the National Administration of Conservation Areas (ANAC), said that the strategy aims to contribute to the awareness of various actors dealing with biodiversity in Mozambique.
“The strategy establishes an audience segmentation of target groups, dividing into groups, namely an internal audience, which is composed of a team from the Ministry of Land and Environment, in general, managers of the conservation areas, employees, management partners from the conservation areas and partners directly involved in the planning and implementation of programs for the protection, conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity, constituting all the actors in the implementation of the communication strategy for the conservation of biodiversity,” Mutemba explained.
Cooperation partners such as USAID and the UNDP have promised support for strengthening nature conservation, with ANAC signing, at the same event, a memorandum of understanding with the National Tourism Institute (INATUR), the National Road Administration (ANE) and Ídolo Magazine for the installation of more panels and the promotion of the country’s biodiversity tourist potential.
By Amandio Borges

a414.t:
Ramallah (UNA/WAFA) - Den officielle talsmand for præsidentskabet, Nabil Abu Rudeina, sagde, at nyhederne cirkuleret af nogle israelske medier om snak om den såkaldte etablering af en bufferzone i den nordlige Gaza-stribe og Jabalia for at distribuere bistand til Gaza-striben gennem et amerikansk privat selskab og med udenlandsk finansiering, er... Planerne er fuldstændigt afvist og uacceptable, og de overtræder alle resolutioner om international legitimitet og international lov, som betragter Gaza-striben som en integreret del af territoriet i Gaza-striben. den besatte stat Palæstina..
Han tilføjede, at alle planer relateret til Gaza-stribens fremtid eller fordeling af bistand der kun laves gennem staten Palæstina og gennem FN's Hjælpe- og Arbejderorganisation for Palæstinensiske Flygtninge (UNRWA) og andre internationale organisationer med jurisdiktion..
Abu Rudeina påpegede, at præsident Mahmoud Abbas gentagne gange understregede nødvendigheden af at implementere FN-resolution nr. 2735 øjeblikkeligt, som opfordrer til et øjeblikkeligt stop for aggressionen mod Gaza-striben, den akutte indtræden af bistand til hele striben, hvis staten Palæstina antager. dets fulde ansvar og den fuldstændige israelske tilbagetrækning fra Gaza-striben.
Han understregede, at eventuelle midlertidige planer ikke vil adressere rødderne til konflikten, som kun vil blive løst ved at implementere den rådgivende udtalelse fra Den Internationale Domstol, der afslutter den israelske besættelse og inkarnerer uafhængigheden af staten Palæstina med Østjerusalem som hovedstad. ..
Det er bemærkelsesværdigt, at de israelske medier talte om en plan, der i øjeblikket overvejes om at etablere en bufferzone i den nordlige Gaza-stribe og Jabalia-lejren, for at bringe bistand ind i Gaza-striben gennem et privat amerikansk sikkerhedsfirma med udenlandsk finansiering, iflg. hvad der blev offentliggjort af de israelske medier..
(jeg er færdig)
a414.en:
The official spokesman for the Palestinian Presidency: Talk of establishing a buffer zone for distributing aid in Gaza is completely rejected — Union of Organisation of Islamic Cooperation News Agencies

Ramallah (UNA/WAFA) — The official spokesman for the Presidency, Nabil Abu Rudeina, said that the news circulated by some Israeli media about talk of the so-called establishment of a buffer zone in the northern Gaza Strip and Jabalia in order to distribute aid to the Gaza Strip through an American private company and with foreign funding is... These plans are completely rejected and unacceptable, and they violate all resolutions of international legitimacy and international law, which consider the Gaza Strip an integral part of the territory of the occupied State of Palestine.

He added that all plans related to the future of the Gaza Strip or the distribution of aid there are made only through the State of Palestine and through the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees (UNRWA) and other international organisations with jurisdiction.

Abu Rudeina pointed out that President Mahmoud Abbas has repeatedly stressed the necessity of implementing UN Resolution No. 2735 immediately, which calls for an immediate halt to the aggression against the Gaza Strip, the urgent entry of aid into the entire Strip, the State of Palestine assuming its full responsibility, and the complete Israeli withdrawal from the Gaza Strip.

He stressed that any temporary plans will not address the roots of the conflict, which will only be solved by implementing the advisory opinion of the International Court of Justice that ends the Israeli occupation and embodies the independence of the State of Palestine with East Jerusalem as its capital.

It is noteworthy that the Israeli media spoke of a plan currently under consideration to establish a buffer zone in the northern Gaza Strip and the Jabalia camp, in order to bring aid into the Gaza Strip through a private American security company with foreign funding, according to what was published by the Israeli media.

(End)

a591.t:
Falta de financiamento para ajuda humanitária ameaça os esforços de Uganda, país que acolhe cerca de 600 refugiados por dia desde o início do ano, a maioria vindo do Sudão do Sul e RDC, devido aos conflitos.
Há cada vez mais refugiados a procurar por segurança no Uganda, um dos maiores países africanos que acolhe os “sem teto”.
Desde o início de 2025, uma média de 600 pessoas por dia chegaram ao país, com a expectativa de que este número chegue a 2 milhões até o final do ano.
Actualmente, Uganda abriga 1,93 milhão de refugiados, dos quais mais de um milhão têm menos de 18 anos. No entanto, a resposta humanitária enfrenta uma das piores crises de financiamento em décadas, segundo as Nações Unidas.
A Diretora de Relações Externas do ACNUR visitou recentemente centros que acolhem refugiados sudaneses e sul-sudaneses em Uganda e alertou que mais crianças morrerão de desnutrição, mais meninas serão vítimas de violência sexual e famílias ficarão sem abrigo ou protecção, a menos que o mundo se mobilizasse, já que o financiamento de emergência pode acabar até Setembro.
A política progressista de refugiados de Uganda permite que os refugiados vivam, trabalhem e tenham acesso a serviços públicos, mas a escassez de financiamento está a impactar drasticamente a prestação de ajuda e ameaça desfazer anos de progresso. Actualmente, os refugiados recebem apenas um terço do que precisam para atender às suas necessidades básicas anualmente.
a591.en:
Uganda at risk of humanitarian crisis

A lack of funding for humanitarian aid threatens the efforts of Uganda, a country that has been taking in around 600 refugees a day since the beginning of the year, most of them coming from South Sudan and the DRC because of conflicts.

More and more refugees are seeking safety in Uganda, one of the largest African countries hosting the "homeless".

Since the beginning of 2025, an average of 600 people a day have arrived in the country, with the expectation that this number will reach 2 million by the end of the year.

Uganda currently hosts 1.93 million refugees, of whom more than one million are under 18. However, the humanitarian response is facing one of the worst funding crises in decades, according to the United Nations.

The Director of External Relations of UNHCR recently visited centres hosting Sudanese and South Sudanese refugees in Uganda and warned that more children will die of malnutrition, more girls will be victims of sexual violence and families will be left without shelter or protection, unless the world mobilises, since emergency funding could run out by September.

Uganda's progressive refugee policy allows refugees to live, work and access public services, but the shortage of funding is drastically affecting the delivery of aid and threatens to undo years of progress. Currently, refugees receive only a third of what they need to meet their basic needs annually.

a609.t:
…Lack of names & presence of two nursing mothers raise eyebrows
The Ghana Prison Service, has come under intense scrutiny, following the amnesty granted to 998 prisoners across the country, amid concerns over transparency and the presence of two nursing mothers among the beneficiaries.
While the Presidency, has framed the mass release as a humanitarian exercise to decongest overcrowded prisons, the absence of a published list of beneficiaries has triggered public debate and speculation, with critics warning of potential security risks to communities where the ex-convicts may return.
The inclusion of two nursing mothers has also sparked controversy, prompting difficult questions about whether prison authorities properly investigated the circumstances surrounding their pregnancies, whether they became pregnant while in custody, or if they became pregnant prior to their convictions.
In a recent high-profile case involving evangelist Patricia Asiedua, alias “Agradaa” or “Evangelist Mama Pat”, the trial judge, Evelyn Asamoah of the Accra Circuit Court, ordered a pregnancy assessment before sentencing; however, it remains unclear whether similar checks were conducted in these cases.
In past amnesty exercises, the identities of beneficiaries were made public, reassuring communities and dispelling rumours, including the inclusion of unapproved beneficiaries.
However, the failure to do so this time prompted speculation that high-profile convicts, including former Capital Bank founder William Ato Essien and Agradaa, might have benefited, though there has been no official confirmation.
The Presidential Spokesperson, Felix Kwakye Ofosu, who issued the statement, had to come out to deny that the two individuals benefited from the amnesty.
William Ato Essien, the former chief executive officer of the now-defunct Capital Bank, was convicted in April 2023 for misapplying liquidity support from the Bank of Ghana and sentenced to 15 years in prison on October 12, 2023.
Agradaa is yet to serve even six months of her 15-year jail term, after being found guilty of two counts of defrauding by false pretences in July this year.
President John Dramani Mahama’s decision, announced on Monday, 18 August 2025, followed recommendations from the Prisons Service Council and consultations with the Council of State, in line with Article 72(1) of the 1992 Constitution. Out of 1,014 inmates proposed, 998 were approved, making it one of the most extensive presidential clemency exercises in recent years.
Figures released by the Presidency indicate that 787 of the beneficiaries are first-time offenders.
In addition, 87 prisoners on death row will have their sentences commuted to life imprisonment, while 51 serving life sentences will have theirs reduced to a fixed term of 20 years.
The list also covers 33 prisoners classified as seriously ill, 36 convicts aged over 70, and the two nursing mothers. Two others were granted clemency on compassionate grounds after their petitions were reviewed.
The government has defended the move as an act of mercy and a pragmatic step towards easing congestion in Ghana’s overburdened correctional system.
But for many Ghanaians, unanswered questions, especially regarding the pregnancies in custody and the secrecy surrounding beneficiaries, have cast a cloud over what should have been a moment of relief and compassion.

a758.t:
Os Estados Unidos pediram às Nações Unidas que congelassem imediatamente a sua contribuição para o fundo destinado a financiar a missão multinacional de ajuda à polícia haitiana, na luta contra as gangues, segundo anunciou, esta quarta-feira, a ONU.
“Recebemos uma notificação oficial dos Estados Unidos da suspensão imediata da sua contribuição (financeira) para a força multinacional de apoio à segurança”, disse Stéphane Dujarric, dando esta notificação como um exemplo do impacto do congelamento geral da ajuda internacional americana, anunciado por Donald Trump.
Em Outubro de 2023, o Conselho de Segurança da ONU tinha dado luz verde à Missão Internacional de Apoio à Segurança (MMAS), liderada pelo Quénia, para ajudar a polícia haitiana, que tinha sido esmagada pela violência das gangues.
A MMAS não é uma força da ONU, mas a ONU criou um fundo voluntário para a financiar, que até à data angariou 110 milhões de dólares, segundo a agência de notícias Lusa.
Com 15 milhões de dólares, os Estados Unidos foram o segundo maior contribuinte para este fundo, atrás do Canadá (63 milhões).
Dos 15 milhões de dólares contribuídos por Washington, 1,7 milhões já foram gastos, disse Stéphane Dujarric, indicando que os restantes 13,3 milhões estão agora “congelados”.
No âmbito do MMAS, apenas cerca de 800 polícias de seis países foram progressivamente destacados desde o verão passado, dos 2500 previstos. Os ataques dos gangues que, segundo a ONU, já controlam 85% da capital, não parecem ter diminuído desde então.
Neste contexto, as autoridades haitianas de transição pedem que a missão seja transformada numa força de paz da ONU.
Logo após a sua tomada de posse, a 20 de Janeiro, o Presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, suspendeu a ajuda externa durante três meses, para permitir uma revisão completa da ajuda, nomeadamente para detetar programas que promovam a diversidade ou o aborto.
No início de Janeiro, a ONU anunciou que mais de 5,6 mil pessoas foram mortas pela violência de gangues. O Escritório de Direitos Humanos documentou 315 linchamentos de membros de gangues e pessoas supostamente associadas; pelo menos 281 casos de alegadas execuções sumárias envolveram unidades policiais especializadas.
A violência de gangues no Haiti fez com que mais de seis milhões de pessoas, quase metade da população, precisem de ajuda humanitária. Mais de um milhão de pessoas estão deslocadas e cerca de dois milhões sofrem de insegurança alimentar grave, incluindo 6 000 pessoas em estado de fome, segundo dados da ONU.
a758.en:
The United States has asked the United Nations to immediately freeze its contribution to the fund intended to finance the multinational mission assisting the Haitian police in the fight against the gangs, the UN announced on Wednesday.

"We have received an official notification from the United States of the immediate suspension of its (financial) contribution to the multinational security support force," said Stéphane Dujarric, citing this notification as an example of the impact of the general freeze on American international aid announced by Donald Trump.

In October 2023, the UN Security Council had given the green light to the Multinational Security Support Mission (MMAS), led by Kenya, to assist the Haitian police, who had been overwhelmed by gang violence.

The MMAS is not a UN force, but the UN created a voluntary fund to finance it, which has so far raised 110 million dollars, according to the news agency Lusa.

With 15 million dollars, the United States was the second-largest contributor to this fund, behind Canada (63 million).

Of the 15 million dollars contributed by Washington, 1.7 million has already been spent, said Stéphane Dujarric, indicating that the remaining 13.3 million is now "frozen".

Under the MMAS, only about 800 police officers from six countries have been gradually deployed since last summer, out of the 2,500 planned. The attacks by the gangs, which according to the UN already control 85% of the capital, do not appear to have diminished since then.

In this context, the Haitian transitional authorities are asking for the mission to be transformed into a UN peacekeeping force.

Immediately after taking office on 20 January, the President of the United States, Donald Trump, suspended foreign aid for three months, to allow a complete review of aid, notably in order to detect programmes promoting diversity or abortion.

At the beginning of January, the UN announced that more than 5,600 people had been killed by gang violence. The Human Rights Office documented 315 lynchings of gang members and people supposedly associated with them; at least 281 cases of alleged summary executions involved specialised police units.

Gang violence in Haiti has left more than six million people, almost half the population, in need of humanitarian assistance. More than one million people are displaced and around two million suffer from severe food insecurity, including 6,000 people in a state of famine, according to UN data.

a952.t:
Dans le cadre de l’initiative solidaire “La Grande Collecte“ 2025, l’Ong Shine Together a réussi à collecter, samedi, 09 août 2025, près de 15 000 vêtements et kits d’hygiène. Des vêtements et kits qui seront distribués aux enfants en situation de rue. La cérémonie de collecte s’est déroulée au Centre Communautaire EYA à Cotonou
Près de 15 000 vêtements et kits d’hygiène collectés par l’Ong Shine Together dans le de l’initiative solidaire “La Grande Collecte“ 2025. Fondée avec pour mission de lutter contre l’exclusion sociale et de contribuer à l’amélioration des conditions de vie des personnes vulnérables, avec un accent particulier sur les enfants en situation de rue et en difficulté au Bénin, l’ONG Shine Together agit depuis 2018 à travers divers projets visant à leur garantir l’accès à l’alimentation, à la santé, à l’éducation et à leur réinsertion sociale et professionnelle. Parmi ces initiatives figure La Grande Collecte, un événement citoyen et solidaire qui réunit chaque année des bénévoles, des partenaires et des citoyens autour d’une mission commune : collecter, trier et redistribuer des vêtements aux enfants vivant dans des conditions précaires. Lors de l’édition précédente en 2024, la toute première, plus de 4000 vêtements avaient pu être collectés, ce qui avait permis d’apporter une aide significative à plusieurs centres d’accueil, confirmant l’impact concret et durable de cette mobilisation collective. Cette deuxième édition 2025 avait pour objectif de collecter 10 000 vêtements en faveur des enfants en situation de grande vulnérabilité. Grâce à une mobilisation exceptionnelle de la communauté, des entreprises partenaires et des institutions, cet objectif a été non seulement atteint mais largement dépassé. Dès les premières heures, bénévoles, familles, entreprises et représentants institutionnels se sont relayés pour déposer, trier et préparer les dons, dans une ambiance festive et chaleureuse rythmée par la musique, les échanges et les sourires. Au total, plus de 200 participants se sont mobilisés, avec plus de 120 donateurs grâce auxquels plus de 14 000 vêtements ont pu être collectés au profit des enfants vivant dans la rue et en situation de grande vulnérabilité. Au cœur de l’initiative, un panel inspirant sur le thème « Enfants en situation de rue : Responsabilité collective et engagement solidaire ». Les échanges ont permis, dans un format ouvert et bienveillant, de réfléchir ensemble aux moyens concrets d’agir collectivement pour un avenir meilleur pour ces enfants. Les dons collectés ont été distribués à plusieurs centres dont : Le Centre Passerelle Porto Novo, Centre Oasis Porto Novo, Centre des Sourds Adjarra, Citoyens des Rues, Centre Maman Marguerite, Terres Rouges Dortoir Filles et Terres Rouges CADJÈHOUN. Cette réussite a été rendue possible grâce au soutien de partenaires engagés ainsi que de nombreux autres acteurs ayant contribué aux collations, à la logistique et à la communication. L’ONG Shine Together adresse ses sincères remerciements à toutes les personnes et structures ayant participé à la réussite de cette édition et rappelle que ses actions se poursuivent tout au long de l’année en faveur de l’éducation, de la protection et de l’inclusion sociale des enfants vulnérables.
M.M
a952.en:
As part of the solidarity initiative “La Grande Collecte” (The Big Collection) 2025, the NGO Shine Together succeeded on Saturday, 9 August 2025 in collecting nearly 15,000 items of clothing and hygiene kits. The clothing and kits will be distributed to street children. The collection ceremony took place at the EYA Community Centre in Cotonou.

Nearly 15,000 items of clothing and hygiene kits were collected by the NGO Shine Together as part of the solidarity initiative “La Grande Collecte” 2025. Founded with the mission of fighting social exclusion and contributing to improving the living conditions of vulnerable people, with a particular emphasis on street children and children in difficulty in Benin, the NGO Shine Together has been active since 2018 through various projects aimed at guaranteeing them access to food, health, education and their social and professional reintegration. Among these initiatives is La Grande Collecte, a civic and solidarity event that each year brings together volunteers, partners and citizens around a common mission: to collect, sort and redistribute clothing to children living in precarious conditions. At the previous edition in 2024, the very first, more than 4,000 items of clothing were collected, which made it possible to provide significant help to several reception centres, confirming the concrete and lasting impact of this collective mobilisation. This second edition in 2025 had the objective of collecting 10,000 items of clothing for children in situations of great vulnerability. Thanks to an exceptional mobilisation of the community, partner companies and institutions, that objective was not only reached but largely exceeded. From the earliest hours, volunteers, families, companies and institutional representatives took turns to drop off, sort and prepare the donations, in a festive and warm atmosphere punctuated by music, conversation and smiles. In total, more than 200 participants took part, with more than 120 donors thanks to whom more than 14,000 items of clothing were collected for the benefit of children living on the street and in situations of great vulnerability. At the heart of the initiative was an inspiring panel on the theme “Street children: collective responsibility and solidarity commitment”. The discussions made it possible, in an open and supportive format, to reflect together on concrete ways of acting collectively for a better future for these children. The donations collected were distributed to several centres including: the Centre Passerelle Porto Novo, Centre Oasis Porto Novo, Centre des Sourds Adjarra, Citoyens des Rues, Centre Maman Marguerite, Terres Rouges Dortoir Filles and Terres Rouges CADJÈHOUN. This success was made possible thanks to the support of committed partners as well as many other actors who contributed to the refreshments, the logistics and the communication. The NGO Shine Together extends its sincere thanks to all the people and organisations that took part in the success of this edition and recalls that its work continues throughout the year in favour of the education, protection and social inclusion of vulnerable children.

M.M

a1437.t:
British actor Idris Elba has told the BBC that he will relocate to Africa within the next decade as part of his plans to support the continent’s movie industry.
The 52-year-old star of the hit series The Wire is behind nascent projects to build a film studio on the Tanzanian islands of Zanzibar as well as one in the Ghanaian capital, Accra.
Born in London, Elba, whose mother is from Ghana and father from Sierra Leone, has a strong attachment to Africa.
He wants to leverage his star power to back its burgeoning film business as he says it is vital that Africans get to tell their own stories.
“I would certainly consider settling down here; not even consider, it’s going to happen,” he said in an interview on the sidelines of an industry meeting in Accra.
“I think [I’ll move] in the next five, 10 years, God willing. I’m here to bolster the film industry – that is a 10-year process – I won’t be able to do that from overseas. I need to be in-country, on the continent.”
But in the spirit of Pan-Africanism he will not commit to living in a specific place.
“I’m going to live in Accra, I’m going to live in Freetown [Sierra Leone’s capital], I’m going to live in Zanzibar. I’m going to try and go where they’re telling stories – that’s really important.”
One goal he does have is to make a film in his studio in Accra one day.
‘Own those stories’
Elba, who played South African anti-apartheid leader Nelson Mandela in the 2013 biopic Long Walk to Freedom, believes that it is vital for Africans to be centre-stage in the entire film-making process. That is in front of the camera, behind the camera and also in financing, distribution, marketing and showing the final product.
He imagines that just as movie audiences around the world know the differences between the US cities of New York and Los Angeles without necessarily ever having visited them, they will one day have a more nuanced understanding of the continent.
“This sector is a soft power, not just across Ghana but across Africa.
“If you watch any film or anything that has got to do with Africa, all you’re going to see is trauma, how we were slaves, how we were colonised, how it’s just war and when you come to Africa, you will realise that it’s not true.
“So, it’s really important that we own those stories of our tradition, of our culture, of our languages, of the differences between one language and another. The world doesn’t know that.”
With Nigeria’s Nollywood producing hundreds of movies a year, films are arguably one of the country’s most successful exports. There is also a tradition, especially in parts of Francophone Africa, of making high-quality films.
Elba has previously recognised the talent in Africa’s film industry, but said the facilities were “lacking”.
A 2022 report from Unesco backed up the actor.
The UN’s cultural agency said that despite “significant growth in production”, the business of film-making across the continent was hindered by issues such as piracy, insubstantial training opportunities and a lack of official film institutions.
Elba believes with the right momentum and involvement of governments willing to create an enabling environment, a virtuous circle can be established.
“We have to invest in our story-telling because when you see me, you see a little version of yourself and that encourages us.”
Source: BBC

a1446.t:
Fangak, Jonglei State (Eye Radio) – At least four civilians, including a nine-month-old child, were killed and 25 wounded in a Saturday airstrike on Old Fangak, which the county commissioner blames on the SSPDF. Maj. Gen. Lul said he would respond when authorized.
Following reports of the bombardment, SSPDF spokesperson Maj. Gen. Lul Ruai Koang told Eye Radio he would respond once authorized to issue an official statement.
Biel Butros Biel, the Commissioner of Fangak County, reported that two military gunships, a drone, and a fixed-wing aircraft attacked the town around 4 a.m.
According to the commissioner, the strikes targeted the heart of Old Fangak, a town known to shelter tens of thousands of displaced civilians and have no military presence.
“They bombed a civilian centre,” Commissioner Biel said in a public statement. “They displaced over 30,000 people. The planes belong to the government of South Sudan.”
Biel confirmed that among the dead are a young woman, two men, and a nine-month-old infant. He added that medical teams are still assessing the full extent of the casualties.
“We have just gathered information from the town that four people died, including a nine-month-old boy, a very young child, a woman, and two young men. They were all killed in the bombardment,” Biel stated.
“So far, we have confirmed that 25 civilians have been wounded, some of whom are in critical condition and remain in severe health.”
He pointed out that the only hospital in Old Fangak, operated by Médecins Sans Frontières (Doctors Without Borders), was also hit in the bombardment. The hospital’s pharmacy was destroyed by fire, leaving the area without its primary source of medical care.
“They bombed the hospital… the pharmacy of MSF has been burned to ashes,” Biel said. “Some of the wounded are in critical condition, and we don’t know how they will survive without medicine.”
Commissioner Biel condemned the assault, emphasizing that Old Fangak has no connection to any military activities. He called for urgent humanitarian assistance and international attention to prevent further civilian suffering.
“We are still gathering information,” Biel said. “But what’s clear is this was an attack on innocent people, not combatants.”
The attack follows a public statement made just one day earlier by a spokesperson for the South Sudan People’s Defense Forces (SSPDF), warning that Fangak and nearby Leer County would be targeted.
On Friday, May 2, SSPDF spokesperson Maj. Gen. Lul Ruai Koang revealed that several barges and boats belonging to a United Nations agency and a Sudanese businessman were hijacked in Leer County, Unity State, and Fangak County, Jonglei State.
Maj Gen Lul accused the SPLM-IO and armed youth known as the White Army of being behind the hijacking and issued a warning to the SPLM-IO in the region.
However, on Saturday, May 3, SPLA-IO spokesperson Col. Lam Paul Gabriel dismissed accusations by the SSPDF that their forces detained barges belonging to the United Nations and private businessmen in Adok.
In a statement, Col. Lam denied any hijacking or extortion, stating that the boats are docked at Adok port for reasons known only to the businessmen involved.
